title: Where to Sit? Equilibrium Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Two kids balance a see-saw. A beam balance comes to rest. A crowbar lifts a heavy stone. When Diya sits on a see-saw with a friend twice as heavy, both at the ends, her side shoots up. Where must the heavy friend sit so they balance? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 6, System of Particles and Rotational Motion) we learn the equilibrium of a rigid body.

On a live motion notebook the see-saw is held level and let go while the readout tracks each weight, lever arm and torque, and a graph shows the net torque falling as the friend moves in until it crosses zero at one metre. A slow-mo replay shows the two torques as it tips. We write the two conditions step by step (zero total force, zero total torque), find the push of the pivot, and reach the principle of moments and the lever rule. Then we see link by link why twice the weight sits at half the distance, compare two forces on one line with a couple, and solve a rod hanging from two strings. Then the exam trap (zero force is not enough), an original JEE Main pattern question on a plank on two supports, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.

In this video:

1:40 The rules in five steps: principle of moments
2:27 Where the friend sits, link by link + pause and think
3:03 Same line vs a couple + pause and think
3:36 Worked example: a rod on two strings
4:11 Exam trap: is zero force enough?
